pairs.subject: guest-execution-bounding
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/curator/process.rs:109 Curator's external work (registry node scripts, headless workers) runs as out-of-process subprocesses with a wall-clock timeout, not as an engine embedded in the host process. A search of src-tauri/src/commands/curator/ for interpreter, guest, quickjs, rhai, wasmtime and 'eval(' found nothing, so the subject's precondition does not hold.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/curator/process.rs:25 This is a deadline on a child node process, which the OS can kill without killing the host. That is the subprocess-lifecycle neighbour's ground, not an in-process engine termination handle.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's scope section names untrusted-extension-host and the register-machine subject as neighbours but not subprocess-lifecycle. A one-line boundary would help: a host that runs guest work in a child process is bounded by that subject, because the OS can kill the child without killing the host. Without that line, a wall-clock timeout on a spawned node script could be mis-scored as terminate-from-outside here.
